name: Timeline for an Attached ADU Addition Project in Los Angeles County

mainEntity.name: What timeline should I realistically expect for an attached ADU addition in Los Angeles County from first contractor meeting to final inspection?
mainEntity.text: What timeline should I realistically expect for an attached ADU addition in Los Angeles County from first contractor meeting to final inspection?

acceptedAnswer.text: Homeowners often underestimate how long an attached ADU addition takes in Los Angeles County. From the first meeting with an ADU additions contractor to final inspection, a realistic range is about 10–18 months. Initial site visits, budgeting, and selecting a contractor usually take 1–2 months. Architectural design, structural engineering, and plan drafting can add 2–4 months, especially if you need multiple revisions to match your budget. Submitting for permits and going through plan check can take another 2–4 months, depending on your jurisdiction’s workload, whether corrections are required, and if any special reviews are triggered by hillside, historic, or flood zones. Once permits are issued, construction for an attached ADU addition often runs 4–7 months, with framing, mechanicals, insulation, and finishes each requiring their own inspection milestones. Unexpected discoveries inside existing walls or foundations can extend this timeline. Final inspections, punch‑list work, and obtaining a certificate of occupancy can add several weeks at the end. To keep the schedule on track, clarify your contractor’s typical duration for similar projects, how they handle plan check comments, and what happens if you request changes after permit approval. Fast decision‑making and clear communication can shave weeks off the process.
